_about: Named test conditions for gameplay_run.py. Each asserts [SHADERS] keys before launch ('_common' plus
its own 'expect'; --expect KEY=VALUE adds or overrides one). The runner never edits the ini: set the keys
with an editor first. A key the ini lacks counts as the build's default from '_defaults' -- update that
block when a new build adds or changes a key (source: ReadConfig in shaderprecompile.ixx, vkcapture.ixx,
shadercapture.ixx). 'dropins' are .bin/.foz files (repo-relative) staged flat into plugins\d3d9cache\ or
plugins\pipelinecache\ as FusionFix.<fnv1a64>.<ext>. 'cold' (default true) empties the Mesa cache first;
--warm / --cold override it. Every measurement condition has capture off (CaptureDrawKeys and
CaptureVulkanPipelines = 0): the snapshot recordings are what gets warmed, and D3D9 capture costs frame
rate. From d3c5dc1 vkcapture hooks vkGetInstanceProcAddr whatever the settings, so the frame times and the
gameplay compile counter are there in every condition, 'off' included (on 141a876 they needed Capture- or
ReplayVulkanPipelines = 1). Gameplay still starts only once a loading screen has come and gone.
_state_files_about: plugins\ files the runner removes before and after a run (globs, never a snapshot recording): FusionFix's
record of the snapshot it last copied into each drop-in folder, and each side's temp file, left behind only
by a crash mid-write. Names read off the merged build d3c5dc1: d3d9cache.h StatePath and WriteFileAtomic,
vkcapture.ixx ShareOwnRecording. Both temp files sit beside the ASI -- the Vulkan side stages its copy as
plugins\FusionFix.pipelinecache.tmp and renames it in, so no stray .tmp lands in the folder players copy.
The runner lists every file it removes in meta.json.
From a532e24 the engine warm phase keeps a fingerprint of (enumeration, driver, DXVK build, shader set) in
FusionFix.enginewarm.stamp and takes a cheap 512-job probe instead of the whole pass when it matches, so
the stamp is state too: a cold run that meets one is not a first launch. It is removed like the others
unless the run passes --keep-state (or the condition sets 'keep_state'), which is how the repeat-launch
arm is measured. PrecompileEmitLog writes FusionFix.enginewarm.emitted.jsonl beside the ASI; it is off in
every measurement condition here, and removed if a run leaves one.

off.about: Nothing warmed: no loading-screen pass, no Vulkan replay, no capture.

d3d9.about: The D3D9 pass only (snapshot capture + shipped baseline).

pass-only.about: The loading-screen pass with NOTHING to warm: PrecompileCoverage = 0 so the synthetic dummy-draw pass returns on its first line, no recorded keys, no Fossilize replay, no engine phase. What is left is the pass itself -- it creates the shader objects, holds the loading screen, and on a gate where it draws its own overlay it also PRESENTS. Read against 'off' (20 pipelines before gameplay, no pass at all), the difference is what the pass's own frames build. That is the arm that separates 'the gate changed what the replay warms' from 'the gate stopped the pass presenting' (2026-09-21).

d3d9+vk-own.about: The D3D9 pass, then this PC's own Fossilize recording; nothing foreign.

full.about: Everything the defaults warm: D3D9 pass, own recording, foreign databases (the player's Steam pre-cache buckets).

full-oldgate.about: 'full' with the warm pass at the OLD loading-screen gate (PrecompileBootGate = 0, from e21a4b9): one blocking call on the first loading screen, presenting its own frames, instead of slices behind the game's. It is the control arm for anything about the gate, and from e21a4b9 it is one ini key rather than a second binary -- which is how the 2026-09-21 comparison had to be made, with the build as a second variable. The number it exists to produce is 'created by DXVK before gameplay': the two gates have to agree, or the replay is still building a different set of pipelines depending on where it runs.

synth.about: The control for 'engine': the same pass with the engine phase OFF, so what is left is the old synthetic dummy-draw pass (PrecompileShaders = 1, PrecompileReplayCapturedKeys = 0). The difference between this and 'engine' is what the engine warm phase is worth on its own.

engine.about: The engine-driven warm phase ALONE: no recorded keys, no Fossilize replay. PrecompileShaders stays 1 because the engine phase runs inside that pass; with PrecompileReplayCapturedKeys = 0 the pass's own work is the old synthetic dummy-draw pass, so this arm is 'engine warm + synthetic', not engine warm in a vacuum.

engine-only.about: The engine-driven warm phase with NOTHING else warming: no recorded D3D9 keys, no Fossilize replay, and PrecompileCoverage = 0 so the old synthetic dummy-draw pass returns immediately (DummyDrawPass's first line). That is what separates this from the 09-20 'engine' arm, where the synthetic pass ran alongside and measured worse than doing nothing. PrecompileShaders stays 1 because the engine phase lives inside that pass; the shader objects it creates (CreateAllShaders) are the only other work left.

full+engine.about: Everything: 'full' (D3D9 replay, own and foreign Fossilize) plus the engine warm phase. From 84a422c the walk builds on a device of its OWN and rotates it every 8192 jobs, which is what keeps the 32-bit address space: PrecompileWarmDevice = 1 is asserted here because it is the whole safety mechanism, and 0 is the arm that killed the game on 2026-09-20.

warm+engine.about: 'full+engine' on a warm Mesa cache, straight after a 'full+engine' run: the floor this build can reach, and the launch that meets the warm fingerprint the run before it left (so it also measures what a repeat load costs). Run the 'full+engine' run before it with --keep-state FusionFix.enginewarm.stamp as well, or its post-run clean takes the stamp away.

engine-abort.about: The safety valve, exercised: 'full+engine' cold with PrecompileGateMaxSeconds = 180, so the gate asks the walk to stop in the middle of a cold pass and the pass has to unwind, hand its warm device back and release the loading screen by itself. That teardown was written for unknown hardware (a walk that would take hours on a slow CPU) and had never been run. It answers two questions at once: whether the abort path really bounds the load and gives the address space back, and whether the engine's render-phase build -- which happens before the walk and is the 2026-09-20 report's second crash candidate -- is survivable on its own with only a few thousand pipelines built.

floor+engine.about: The warm FLOOR of the engine arm, and the third of the three loads a player can meet: warm Mesa cache but NO fingerprint stamp, so the whole walk runs again on a driver that already has every pipeline. That is what a player gets when the stamp is lost but the driver cache is not (a mod update that does not change the shader set, a stamp deleted by hand). 'warm+engine' is the same cache WITH the stamp (the cheap path); this is the same settings without it.

full+win-d3d9.about: 'full' plus the Windows PC's D3D9 capture dropped in the way a player would.

warm.about: 'full' on a warm Mesa cache: the best case.

ini-here.about: The ini exactly as deployed on this machine (/tmp/ff-tools/ini.pristine, D3D9 capture on). For validating the rig, not for measuring.
